newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Holiday-hit Australia bonds kept to range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Holiday-hit Australia bonds kept to range.

text.p: *Australian bond futures contracts showed modest gains in limited turnover during a shortened SYCOM session due to the U.S. and U.K. market holidays on Monday.
*Q1 capital expenditure data at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bond futures contracts showed modest gains in limited turnover during a shortened SYCOM session due to the U.S. and U.K. market holidays on Monday.
The June 10-year bond futures ended the afterhours session at 92.400 compared with Monday's 92.380 pit close and remained contained within its expected short-term 92.330 to 92.410 range.

A brief flirtation to 92.420 during Monday's session as the market attempted to break back to Friday's post-rate cut high of 92.500 proved short-lived, while traders expect the low-92.300s to be supportive.

The market kicks off a fairly busy data week with the release of first quarter capital expenditure at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Forecasts centre on a 3.5 percent rise after the 2.4 percent fall in the December quarter, according to a Reuters survey of economists.
Of more importance will be the second estimate for investment spending in 1997/98 as a clue to future growth.

The U.S. market returns later today to face April consumer confidence and existing home sales, although this week's auctions of two- and five-year notes on Wednesday and Thursday are likely to be the key events.
